answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by requiring each agent to mirror a unique cryptographic signal into a communal harbor of attested identities. Peers verify that the signal matches the agents claimed stake and activity history; fake agents fail because they cannot continuously produce matching signals without controlling real compute resources that are already claimed by legitimate participants. This binding of identity to verifiable output raises the cost of creating disposable identities far above the expected gain.
